title: Hosted API demo - chat & text generation (Halo Markets)
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming, generation params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retries and idempotency, rate limits and basic security questions. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a low-latency trading assistant use case.
transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen, Omar Ruiz, Anita Park (Redwood) - Liam O'Donnell, Priya Kapoor, Sara Gomez (Halo Markets)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, and with me is Omar on the SE side and Anita on product. How's everyone doing?
[00:03] Liam O'Donnell: Good, thanks. Excited to see the hosted API flow.
[00:06] Priya Kapoor: Quick note, we have like 30 minutes of deep questions from infra side, so Omar, heads up.
[00:09] Omar Ruiz: Yep, totally - we'll leave time.

[02:15] Maya Chen: Quick agenda: demo of hosted API for chat/text gen, walk through streaming, parameters you can tweak, retries/timeout behavior, and then Q&A on security and latency. Does that sound good?
[02:22] Sara Gomez: Yep. Also want to confirm data residency and KMS options.

[04:30] Omar Ruiz: Alright I'll share screen - bear with me, I've got the Redwood Console open - apologies if the product name shows as Redwood Infer in one widget, small UI bug. So first, this is the hosted API endpoint, simple REST and SDKs. For chat we use a messages array, for text gen a prompt param.
[04:45] Liam O'Donnell: Do you have support for streaming tokens back? We need to render incremental answers in our trading UI.
[04:51] Omar Ruiz: Yes - streaming is supported. You can do event-stream chunked responses over HTTP/1.1 and via websockets in some SDKs. Example curl: "curl -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'" and you'll receive partial tokens as they generate. Note that with streaming we maintain the same cost model - tokens streamed count as generated tokens.
[05:23] Priya Kapoor: Any eventual consistency concerns with KV cache or prefix caching when streaming?
[05:27] Omar Ruiz: Good question - the hosted runtime does prefix/KV caching automatically for repeated context. For streaming it's mostly independent - cache helps reduce compute for repeated prefixes but doesn't change token ordering. There's an edge case where the first streaming response might be slightly slower if cache is warming.

[07:00] Maya Chen: Let's demo parameters - temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences. I'll pull up a quick example in the SDK.
[07:10] Anita Park: Also show n and logprobs? Some teams like n=3 for diversity.
[07:14] Omar Ruiz: Right. Example payload: temperature 0.2 for conservative answers; top_p 0.9; max_tokens 256. For deterministic behavior we recommend 0.0-0.2 temp for trade-adjacent guidance.
[07:35] Liam O'Donnell: For our use case we need reproducible outputs for some prompts; is there a way to reduce randomness further?
[07:40] Omar Ruiz: Two levers: set temperature to near zero and set top_p to 0.0 or very low, and pin model version. Also keep max_tokens deterministic. We also offer deterministic sampling mode on certain model variants - that's more common on our dedicated offering but some hosted models support it.

[09:05] Priya Kapoor: How do you handle retries? If a request times out mid-generation, what's recommended?
[09:11] Omar Ruiz: We recommend idempotency keys for any non-idempotent requests. For chat inserts we provide a request_id header; our SDKs auto-retry idempotent operations. For generation, you can set a client-side timeout and then retry with the same idempotency key - Redwood will detect duplicate and either resume or return same output depending on timing and model variant.
[09:40] Sara Gomez: So that means we won't double-bill if a client retries?
[09:44] Omar Ruiz: Correct in most cases - retries with same idempotency key are deduped server-side, though if the original completed but the client didn't receive it there's a small risk of duplicate billing; we have safeguards and you can opt-in for stronger exactly-once guarantees via reserved capacity.

[11:30] Maya Chen: Let's talk rate limits and quotas - hosted customers get per-minute token rate limits and per-account quotas. We can show quota metrics in the console.
[11:39] Anita Park: Also mention soft vs hard limits - soft limits can be raised.
[11:43] Liam O'Donnell: For our trading assistants, tail latency is critical - we need <150ms p50 and p95 under 500ms for short responses. Can hosted meet that?
[11:52] Omar Ruiz: Depends on model size and prompt length. For small-context prompts and lighter models, p50 can be under 100ms in our nearest region; p95 varies. For strict SLOs we typically recommend Dedicated or pinned smaller models. We do have performance profiles per model in the catalog.
[12:20] Priya Kapoor: If we go hosted, is there routing by region? We have EU and us-east customers.
[12:25] Omar Ruiz: Yes - you can pin region and we route to the closest region; we also support multi-region fallback.

[14:00] Maya Chen: Quick note on cost - you can optimize with batching and caching and quantized model variants. Redwood Optimize will give suggestions automatically for batching thresholds.
[14:10] Liam O'Donnell: Can that run as part of hosted or only in Dedicated?
[14:13] Anita Park: Redwood Optimize operates across hosted and dedicated; for hosted we give recommendations and you can enable automatic batching in the SDK. For dedicated you get more control.

[16:00] Maya Chen: Alright demo time - I'll make a sample request in the console to show streaming and parameter tweaks. (typing noises)
[16:12] Omar Ruiz: Note the console shows token-level time and cost, and you can replay responses. Small transcription glitch sometimes shows product names as Redwood Ui.
[17:05] Maya Chen: Here's a streaming response - you can see partial tokens printed to the console. That can integrate with your frontend easily.
[17:20] Priya Kapoor: Looks good. Can we get request traces into our tracing system?
[17:24] Omar Ruiz: Yes we emit trace IDs and you can map them to your tracing via headers; we also support trace export to Datadog and Zipkin via sinks in the console.

[19:00] Liam O'Donnell: Security questions: SOC2, encryption, KMS, SSO, VPC options.
[19:06] Maya Chen: We're SOC2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. For encryption, hosted uses server-side encryption and can offer bring-your-own-key in certain enterprise plans; Private supports customer-managed keys and HSMs. SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC are supported.
[19:30] Sara Gomez: For data retention, can you disable retention or set short TTLs?
[19:34] Anita Park: Hosted has configurable retention windows; enterprise customers can opt for no retention or encrypted ephemeral storage for compliance.

[21:15] Priya Kapoor: Any mention of competitors - we've also looked at OpenAI and Vertex. How's latency/cost versus those?
[21:21] Omar Ruiz: Broadly, Redwood focuses on production economics - comparable latency on similar models, but we offer more control for routing, caching and cost levers. Against OpenAI you get more deterministic stack controls; against Vertex you might have closer cloud integration, but Redwood gives a unified runtime with Optimize tooling.

[23:00] Maya Chen: Ok next I'll show a simple retry demo - I'll intentionally set a short timeout and show idempotency header. (demo) If the request fails we retry with the same idempotency key and you can see we get a deduped result.
[23:40] Priya Kapoor: Nice. Any SDKs for node/python/java?
[23:44] Omar Ruiz: Yes official SDKs for Node, Python and Java plus gRPC in beta. The SDKs handle retries, batching, and streaming helpers.

[26:10] Liam O'Donnell: For POC sizing: we expect 500k tokens/day initially, peak bursts to 2M tokens/day, and lots of short prompts (~20-80 tokens). Will that fit hosted?
[26:22] Maya Chen: Hosted can handle that for a trial; we'd recommend a short pilot to observe tail latencies. If you need capacity guarantees, Dedicated reserved capacity would be next.
[26:40] Sara Gomez: For compliance we may need VPC or Private later - is that supported?
[26:45] Anita Park: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options and you can bring your KMS/HSM.

[29:00] Maya Chen: Toward the end, summarizing - hosted can get you going fast with streaming and param control; retries with idempotency keys; Optimize suggestions for batching; for strict latency we recommend a path to Dedicated.

[30:10] Liam O'Donnell: Good recap. Let's talk next steps.
[30:15] Priya Kapoor: We'll need security docs and a sample curl and maybe a short benchmark script we can run.
[30:20] Maya Chen: Sure. We'll send SOC2, encryption/KMS docs, and a small benchmark harness and example curl. Omar will provide SE benchmark notes.

[32:00] Omar Ruiz: Also I'll include a script that simulates your token distribution and shows expected p50/p95 for a couple model variants.

[33:30] Sara Gomez: And we'll send over our expected workload distribution and latency SLOs.

[35:00] Maya Chen: Any blockers or open concerns?
[35:05] Priya Kapoor: Main concern is tail latency on hosted, and exact billing behavior on retries.
[35:12] Omar Ruiz: We'll document retry billing behavior in the benchmark notes and show the idempotency behavior.

[40:00] Maya Chen: Final recap and next steps - we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2, benchmark script and a proposed pilot start date.
[40:10] Liam O'Donnell: Proposed pilot start 2026-12-27 if we get NDA and pilot access.
[40:15] Maya Chen: That works. Thanks everyone.
[40:25] (meeting ends)
